work_and_reuse_rules.excerpt: work done outside of the hacking period
work_and_reuse_rules.meaning: The event disallows submitted project work completed outside its hacking period; event-created work required.

work_and_reuse_rules.excerpt: document any external code usage in your submission and mention them during judging
work_and_reuse_rules.meaning: Libraries, frameworks and open-source code are explicitly allowed with attribution in the submission and during judging, distinguishing team contributions.
One project per team. The submitted project may not be submitted to other hackathons.
MLH Code of Conduct applies; this is not evidence adopting separate general MLH competition policies.

The short rule page does not explain whether pre-event planning/research notes or curated data are treated as disallowed project work. Preserve source/creation history, build fresh application code during the event, and disclose prior research rather than claiming it was created at the event. Sponsor-supplied data is explicitly intended for this proof of concept per user-provided Sperry clarification.

guide_support.summary: Official supplied guide advertises an INIT Codex workshop building applications with an AI coding agent and an MLH GitHub Copilot coding workshop.

ai.conclusion: AI development tools are openly contemplated by event programming; no blanket AI ban found. Exact AI disclosure wording, permitted scope, or a dedicated disclosure field is not stated in accessed public rules.
ai.implementation_practice: Document AI assistance, libraries and external code in README/submission, review generated work, and distinguish original team contributions. This is a prudent disclosure practice, not an invented explicit AI-specific event requirement.

submission_checklist.item: Team has at most four hackers.
Submit one project on Devpost; one member creates it and invites all teammates before submission.
Use the same email used for ShellHacks registration; include first/last names in accounts or submission comments.
Include at least one Discord tag so judges can contact the team.
Select prize categories before deadline, including Sperry; multiple challenges are allowed for the same single project. General best-overall consideration is automatic.
Document external code in submission and mention it during judging.
Prepare a three-minute in-person live demo; possible round-two demo is three to five minutes. Be at the assigned location by 1pm per Discord table/room announcement.
Finish hacking and submit before September 27 at 11am EDT; reserve upload/verification buffer.
